modules.comments:
SMTLib2 surface syntax: atoms and lists, nothing else. Atoms are
kept raw — a string literal is an atom that includes its quotes,
a |quoted symbol| includes its pipes. `print` is the wire format;
`feed`/`finish` is a streaming parser for chunked solver stdout.

declarations.comments:
Streaming parser state. Feed chunks as they arrive from the
solver; completed toplevel forms fall out of each `feed`.
declarations.title: ParseState

declarations.comments:
End of input: flush a trailing toplevel atom, reject anything
left half-open.
declarations.title: finish

modules.name: Mycroft.SExpr

modules.comments:
The typed veneer: untyped `Term`s built by smart constructors,
simple-smt style. Enough SMTLib2 for finite-domain work — enum
sorts, Int arithmetic for cardinality, uninterpreted functions,
named assertions, models, unsat cores.

declarations.comments: Constant assignments from `get-model`: name ↦ value s-expression.
declarations.title: Model

declarations.comments:
(declare-datatypes ((Name 0)) (((c1) (c2) …))) — a nullary
datatype, i.e. an enumeration.
declarations.title: declareEnum

declarations.comments:
(assert (! t :named n)) — named assertions are what unsat cores
are made of.
declarations.title: assertNamed

declarations.comments:
Run an action inside a push/pop scope; the pop happens even if
the action throws.
declarations.title: inNewScope

declarations.comments:
How many of the given terms equal the target — the sum-of-ite
cardinality encoding, for hand-size style constraints.
declarations.title: countEq

declarations.comments:
Read a model value that should be a bare atom (an Int literal or
an enum constructor).
declarations.title: lookupAtom

modules.name: Mycroft.SmtLib

modules.comments:
The session layer: a solver kept in lockstep. The simple-smt trick
— set `:print-success` immediately, so every command produces
exactly one response s-expression and framing is trivial: write one
form, read one form.

The transport is abstracted: `newSolver` speaks to a subprocess
(`z3 -in -smt2` by default); other backends (the WASM build, a
remote solver) supply their own `Transport` via `newSolverWith`
and inherit the whole veneer above this module unchanged.

declarations.comments:
What a backend receives: where to deliver solver output (chunked,
any framing) and where to report a dead backend.
declarations.title: Callbacks

declarations.comments:
What a backend provides: write one line of SMTLib2, and tear the
backend down (called at most once, by `stop`).
declarations.title: Transport

declarations.comments: Bring up a solver over any transport and put it in lockstep mode.
declarations.title: newSolverWith

declarations.comments:
Send one command, await its one response. Lockstep discipline:
callers issue one command at a time (all the veneer functions do).
declarations.title: command

declarations.comments: A command whose only acceptable response is the atom `success`.
declarations.title: ackCommand

modules.name: Mycroft.Solver

packageMeta.description: A thin SMT solver wrapper in the style of Haskell's simple-smt: s-expressions in, s-expressions out, a lockstep process session, and a small SMTLib veneer — named assertions, models, unsat cores.
packageMeta.name: purescript-mycroft
